# Native widget installation evidence

`mluva-install-widget` ports the released bundle staging, ownership and upgrade transaction into Rust. It is an explicit installation tool, separate from the resident app. `--stage DIRECTORY` prepares an archive widget without desktop contact; `--check` stages privately, checks existing ownership and runs Omarchy's schema validator without changing the installed plugin. Normal installation preserves the content-addressed QML entry point, manifest, receipt hashes, private backup and asynchronous rescan/discovery/enable sequence. Clean published legacy Git checkouts migrate without fetching their retired remotes. Local edits, untracked files, unpublished commits, foreign origins, links and duplicate identities are preserved and refused.

Build with `cargo build --locked -p mluva-install --bin mluva-install-widget`. The production layout is `<bundle>/bin/mluva-install-widget` beside `<bundle>/manifest.json` and `<bundle>/linux/quickshell/mluva.dictation/`. The executable resolves that actual package location, including when launched through a symlink, and has no source-checkout fallback. The tested ELF links only libc and libgcc; no GTK, interpreter, Python library or compatibility process is involved. [Native runtime assembly](package-evidence.md) now supplies this layout; switching the existing installation entry points remains separate work.

The immutable source is v1.6.0, commit `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The released `linux/install_widget.py` SHA-256 is `66fa46989416951deb2396f33010beeeee5175d973779b592acda2be35c53f3e`; the root manifest is `94decd83fcc56d5ed5ee1cdd29ba3ecc065de02e26b8d399bf6fd8b652d7728c`. Both were checked against the immutable Git blobs. Current QML/font assets and manifest still match that commit. The external collector runs the actual released CLI in copied archives and does not replace installer functions or filesystem operations. Its temporary Python observer remains outside the maintained tree in ignored `tmp/`.

[The frozen fixture](released-widget.json), SHA-256 `9916693a4b16025c88227a092cdfa946476262a5d2f69fc8508ebfec51b9e72c`, contains 71 transactions and 98 observed states. The original 54 transactions were captured before native comparisons; 17 independently observed CLI cases were appended without changing those results. Cases exercise clean/staged/check-only installs, nested staging paths, Unicode content, unchanged and changed updates, renamed bundles, local modifications and symlinks, all three accepted Git origins and unpublished/dirty/foreign histories, validation/rescan/discovery/enable failures, delayed discovery, the real forty-attempt timeout, invalid source identity/JSON/entry points, help, option aliases/equals/duplicates and usage errors.

The maintained Rust comparison executes the actual relocated ELF for every operation, with separate private HOME, temporary directories and environment. A small separate Bash peer supplies only the external shell registry and chosen failures. Every validation call runs the actual installed `omarchy-plugin-validate`, pinned by SHA-256 `f7507e5042eb970e3dc918bdf6bf251c7557443892a77e71a17d7019ddde72c8`. Real local Git repositories are initialized, committed, cloned and inspected without network access. The peer never contacts Omarchy's running shell or a session bus. It has no production injection seam and is not a distribution asset.

Comparisons cover exit status, success/help/usage output, ownership refusal text, command order/arguments and full installed/staged/backup file hashes and modes. Existing receipt and QML manifest bytes, including Unicode escaping and content-addressed bundle names, match exactly. Normalization removes only disposable path prefixes/random directory names and replaces the reference CLI's executable basename. OS exception spelling, JSON parser wording and failed-subprocess diagnostic details are compared as explicit failure categories; native messages bound these diagnostics instead of reproducing interpreter details. Source/receipt parser input is never echoed. Filesystem timestamps and Git's stat cache are not compatibility assertions. Git internals are omitted from portable fixture trees, but a separate before/after comparison verifies all local Git history/configuration bytes and modes except its mutable index across retention or migration.

The first native comparison failed because `--stage` did not create missing parents (`tmp/widget-native-first.log`). After that repair, the upgrade comparison exposed default temporary-directory permissions of 0755 instead of the released 0700 (`tmp/widget-native.log`). All staging and backup roots now request 0700 at creation. The first expanded CLI comparison failed the help contract (`tmp/widget-cli-before.log`); the native parser now preserves the compared help, mutual exclusion, aliases and statuses. These failures remain recorded; their frozen expectations were not weakened.

Two additional actual-process faults test a destination appearing before promotion and a promoted destination being replaced before rollback. The unchanged reference deletes the unrelated replacement in both faults, observed separately in `tmp/widget-fault-reference-evidence/` and `tmp/widget-fault-reference.log`; these are not recorded as matched behavior. The initial native implementation already preserved the failed-promotion collision but failed the replaced-destination case in `tmp/widget-ownership-before.log`. The repaired rollback checks the installed directory's device/inode before removal. A foreign replacement remains untouched, and the previous widget is either restored under its original name or retained in its private backup with a specific recovery diagnostic. This deliberate data-preservation repair does not claim adversarial race immunity, crash recovery or signal-safe transactions.

Run the explicit comparison in the guarded environment:

```sh
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/native-widget-install -- \
  cargo test --locked -p mluva-install --test widget -- \
  --ignored --nocapture
```

The accepted final run is `tmp/widget-final-evidence/` with `tmp/widget-final.log`: all 71 reference transactions/98 states and both native ownership faults pass. The full ordinary workspace passes 137 tests with zero failures and 43 environment-dependent tests ignored in `tmp/widget-workspace.log`; this widget test was explicitly executed as above. Strict all-target Clippy passes in `tmp/widget-clippy.log`, and formatting, diff and ShellCheck checks pass. Earlier reference runs are retained in `tmp/widget-reference-evidence/` and `tmp/widget-cli-reference-evidence/`. Builds/tests were allowed to finish before every source, fixture or test edit.

This evidence establishes private filesystem installation behavior and the real manifest schema contract. The [native application installer](install-evidence.md) and [uninstaller](uninstall-evidence.md) now have separate disposable-prefix evidence. Actual Quickshell discovery, enable/layout persistence and visual hot reload with the native bridge remain required. Legacy VoiceScribe migration, final production archive/entry-point selection, maintained/shipped Python removal and whole-application/platform/performance acceptance remain pending. No installed app/widget, user settings or visible desktop was changed; the working release remains 1.6.0.
